To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the immunodetection and DNA probing approaches for detection of schistosomes in snails have potential for facilitating rapid evaluation of the risk of post-control schistosomiasis reinfection, and that further evaluation of these approaches for facilitating catalytic representation of schistosomia-snail epidemiology is warranted.

immunodetection of schistosomal antigen(s) in snail hemolympth, and dot hybridziation of snail extracts with a DNA probe representing repeated sequences, proved useful for detecting infected snail populations during prepatency.
immunodetection and DNA probing are suitable for detecting schistosome-infested snails during pre-patency as well as during patency.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of immunodiagnostic tests for the detection of schistosomal infections in the intermediate host snail, and the application of these tests for the epidemiological evaluation of schistosome control measures.
the development of immunodiagnostic approaches for detecting schistosomal infection in snails.

the development of new diagnostic approaches that are potentially suitable for large scale application, for the detection of schistosome infection in snails, and for providing extended information that may facilitate rapid and cost-effective decisions on control measures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
immunodetection by the ELISA approach is a suitable and potentially useful approach for the large scale detection of schistosome infected snails.

the immunodetection of schistosomal antigen in the hemolymph of infected snails is a suitable approach for large scale screening for schistosomal infections in snails, but not for specific identification of S. mansoni or S. haematubium infections.
both the immunodetection and DNA probing approaches are potentially suitable and complementary for providing extended information that can help make more informed decisions on schistosome control.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the detection of schistosome antigens and DNA in snails provides a valuable tool for epidemiological studies, and may prove useful for the detection of schistsomal infections in snails for the purposes of schistosome control.
immunodetection of schistosomal infection in snails is a promising approach for facilitating epidemiologic studies of schistosome transmission.

immunodetection of schistosomal hemolymph antigens by ELISA, and dot hybridizations of snails by DNA probes are potentially useful for detecting schistosome-infested snails during pre- as well as patent schistosomal infection, and may be of value for epidemiological studies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
immunodiagnosis and DNA probing are potentially useful for detecting prepatently infected snails, which is important for the evaluation of the danger and extent of post-control reinfections.
the immunodetection and DNA probing approach are suitable for detecting snail infection with schistosomes during the prepatent phase.
the immunological detection approach is the most promising for large scale detection and identification of snails pre- and postpatently infected with schistosomes.
